findings.evidence: Lines 104, 116, 131, 146, 161, and 176 conclude `pdf X P =ᵐ[...] <family>PDF ...`; the naming guide requires conclusions first and hypotheses after `of`, as in Mathlib's `integral_of_hasLaw_binomial`.
findings.fix: Rename them following the convention that hypotheses follow `of`, e.g. `pdf_eq_gammaPDF_of_hasLaw_gammaMeasure`, `pdf_eq_betaPDF_of_hasLaw_betaMeasure`, and analogously for the other four families.
findings.issue: `pdf_gammaMeasure_eq`, `pdf_betaMeasure_eq`, `pdf_expMeasure_eq`, `pdf_paretoMeasure_eq`, `pdf_gaussianReal_eq`, and `pdf_cauchyMeasure_eq` do not read from their conclusions outward: the measure name occurs only in a `HasLaw` hypothesis, while the concluded PDF name is omitted.

summary: The six density-identification theorem names describe the law hypothesis as though it were part of the equality and omit the actual right-hand-side density.
